Name: basListHelpers
VbaCode:
Option Compare Database
Option Explicit

' ============================================================================
'  basListHelpers
' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
'  Reusable helpers for the "list-box-instead-of-datasheet-subform" pattern.
'
'  Each list box that participates in this pattern follows these conventions:
'
'    - Column 1 is the primary key. It is hidden (ColumnWidth = 0) and is
'      the BoundColumn (so .Value returns the PK).
'    - Columns 2..N are the visible display columns.
'    - ColumnHeads = True; column captions come from the data SELECT's
'      column aliases (because the data SELECT is the FIRST select in the
'      UNION ALL).
'    - A synthetic "<Add new ...>" row is UNION ALL'd onto the data SELECT
'      with PK = ADD_NEW_ID (-1). It sorts to the top because ORDER BY 1
'      (the PK) puts -1 ahead of any real autonumber PK.
'
'  When the user double-clicks a row:
'
'    - If the bound value is ADD_NEW_ID, the detail form opens with
'      OpenArgs = "ADD"  (or "ADD|ClientID=123|FiscalYear=2025" if the
'      caller passes context). This signals the detail form to enter
'      Add mode and disable its Delete button.
'    - Otherwise the detail form opens with OpenArgs = "<numericID>",
'      meaning Edit mode for that record.
'
'  The detail form is opened acDialog so the parent form blocks until
'  the user closes it; we then Requery the list box.
' ============================================================================

' Sentinel PK value for the synthetic "Add New" row.
Public Const ADD_NEW_ID As Long = -1

' A 1-row "DUAL" derivation for the synthetic Add-New SELECT.
' MSysObjects is always present and always non-empty in an Access database.
Private Const DUAL_FROM As String = " FROM (SELECT TOP 1 1 AS X FROM MSysObjects) AS dual "


' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
' Builds the synthetic SELECT that becomes the "<Add new ...>" row.
'   addLabel       e.g. "<Add new service need...>"
'   dataColCount   total column count in the data SELECT (must match)
'
' Column 1 emits ADD_NEW_ID (the bound PK).
' Column 2 emits addLabel (what the user sees).
' Columns 3..N emit Null.
'
' No column aliases are emitted; the union picks up its column captions
' from the data SELECT (the FIRST select in the UNION ALL).
' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Public Function BuildAddRowSelect(addLabel As String, dataColCount As Long) As String
    Dim parts() As String
    Dim i As Long

    If dataColCount < 2 Then
        Err.Raise vbObjectError + 2001, "BuildAddRowSelect", _
                  "dataColCount must be at least 2 (PK + display)."
    End If

    ReDim parts(0 To dataColCount - 1)
    parts(0) = CStr(ADD_NEW_ID)
    parts(1) = "'" & Replace(addLabel, "'", "''") & "'"
    For i = 2 To dataColCount - 1
        parts(i) = "Null"
    Next i

    BuildAddRowSelect = "SELECT " & Join(parts, ", ") & DUAL_FROM
End Function


' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
' Wraps a data SELECT with a synthetic Add-New row (UNION ALL).
'   dataSelect     The user's normal SELECT, including FROM/WHERE.
'                  MUST include explicit aliases on the columns ? those
'                  aliases become the listbox column headers.
'                  MUST NOT include ORDER BY (pass that via orderBy).
'                  Column 1 of the SELECT MUST be the numeric PK.
'   addLabel       What the synthetic row's display column shows.
'   dataColCount   Number of columns the SELECT returns.
'   orderBy        Optional ORDER BY clause (default: "1" = PK; -1 sorts
'                  first ahead of positive autonumber PKs).
' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Public Function BuildAddableRowSource(dataSelect As String, _
                                       addLabel As String, _
                                       dataColCount As Long, _
                                       Optional orderBy As String = "1") As String
    Dim sql As String
    sql = "(" & dataSelect & ") UNION ALL (" & _
          BuildAddRowSelect(addLabel, dataColCount) & ")"
    If Len(orderBy) > 0 Then sql = sql & " ORDER BY " & orderBy
    BuildAddableRowSource = sql
End Function


' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
' Standard double-click handler for a list box that follows the
' "PK in column 1 + Add-New synthetic row" convention.
'
'   lst              The list box the user double-clicked.
'   detailFormName   The popup detail form to open.
'   contextOpenArgs  Optional pipe-delimited "key=value|key=value" pairs
'                    to append to the OpenArgs in Add mode (e.g. to give
'                    the detail form the parent ClientID/FiscalYear so
'                    it can populate FK columns on the new record).
'                    Ignored in Edit mode.
'
' Opens the detail form acDialog (modal) so this Sub blocks until the
' user closes it; then Requery's the list box.
' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Public Sub OpenDetailFromList(lst As Access.ListBox, _
                               detailFormName As String, _
                               Optional contextOpenArgs As String = "")
    Dim selVal As Variant
    selVal = lst.Value
    If IsNull(selVal) Then Exit Sub

    Dim args As String
    If CLng(selVal) = ADD_NEW_ID Then
        args = "ADD"
        If Len(contextOpenArgs) > 0 Then args = args & "|" & contextOpenArgs
    Else
        args = CStr(CLng(selVal))
    End If

    DoCmd.OpenForm detailFormName, acNormal, , , , acDialog, args

    ' Modal closed; refresh the list to reflect any inserts/edits/deletes.
    lst.Requery
End Sub


' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
' Builds an "ADD|key1=val1|key2=val2..." OpenArgs string.
' Pass alternating key, value, key, value, ... in pairs.
' If no pairs are passed, returns "ADD".
'
'   BuildAddOpenArgs("ClientID", 42, "FiscalYear", 2025)
'     -->  "ClientID=42|FiscalYear=2025"
'
' (Caller typically passes the result to OpenDetailFromList's
'  contextOpenArgs parameter, which prepends "ADD|".)
' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Public Function BuildContextArgs(ParamArray pairs() As Variant) As String
    Dim n As Long
    n = UBound(pairs) - LBound(pairs) + 1
    If n = 0 Then Exit Function
    If n Mod 2 <> 0 Then
        Err.Raise vbObjectError + 2002, "BuildContextArgs", _
                  "Pairs must come in key,value couples (got " & n & " items)."
    End If

    Dim parts() As String
    ReDim parts(0 To (n \ 2) - 1)
    Dim i As Long, j As Long
    j = 0
    For i = LBound(pairs) To UBound(pairs) Step 2
        parts(j) = CStr(pairs(i)) & "=" & CStr(pairs(i + 1))
        j = j + 1
    Next i
    BuildContextArgs = Join(parts, "|")
End Function


' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
'  OpenArgs parsing helpers, for use by popup detail forms.
'
'  A popup detail form's Form_Load typically does:
'
'     If basListHelpers.IsAddMode(Me.OpenArgs) Then
'         DoCmd.GoToRecord , , acNewRec
'         Me!ClientID    = basListHelpers.GetContextLong(Me.OpenArgs, "ClientID")
'         Me!FiscalYear  = basListHelpers.GetContextLong(Me.OpenArgs, "FiscalYear")
'         Me.btnDelete.Enabled = False
'     ElseIf IsNumeric(Nz(Me.OpenArgs, "")) Then
'         Dim rs As DAO.Recordset
'         Set rs = Me.RecordsetClone
'         rs.FindFirst "<PKfield>=" & CLng(Me.OpenArgs)
'         If Not rs.NoMatch Then Me.Bookmark = rs.Bookmark
'     End If
' ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

' Returns True iff the OpenArgs string indicates Add mode (starts with "ADD").
Public Function IsAddMode(args As Variant) As Boolean
    Dim s As String
    s = Nz(args, "")
    IsAddMode = (Left$(s, 3) = "ADD")
End Function

' Looks up a key in an "ADD|key1=val1|key2=val2..." OpenArgs string.
' Returns the value as a String, or "" if the key isn't present.
Public Function GetContextString(args As Variant, key As String) As String
    Dim s As String
    s = Nz(args, "")
    If Len(s) = 0 Then Exit Function

    Dim parts() As String
    parts = Split(s, "|")

    Dim i As Long
    Dim prefix As String
    prefix = key & "="
    For i = LBound(parts) To UBound(parts)
        If Left$(parts(i), Len(prefix)) = prefix Then
            GetContextString = Mid$(parts(i), Len(prefix) + 1)
            Exit Function
        End If
    Next i
End Function

' Same as GetContextString but coerces to Long. Returns 0 if missing/blank.
Public Function GetContextLong(args As Variant, key As String) As Long
    Dim raw As String
    raw = GetContextString(args, key)
    If Len(raw) = 0 Then Exit Function
    If IsNumeric(raw) Then GetContextLong = CLng(raw)
End Function
Public Sub PopulateAddableListBoxFromAdo(lst As Access.ListBox, _
                                           sql As String, _
                                           addLabel As String)
    ' Populates a list box via ADO + ListBox.AddItem (Value List row source type).
    '
    ' Use this instead of BuildAddableRowSource when you need a sort order Jet's
    ' UNION-ORDER-BY parser won't reliably deliver, expect more rows than fit in
    ' a RowSource string (~32 KB ceiling), or want column-by-column control.
    '
    '   lst        ListBox to populate. RowSourceType MUST be "Value List".
    '              ColumnCount must match the number of columns the SQL returns.
    '              ColumnHeads = True is supported (the first AddItem call below
    '              becomes the header row).
    '   sql        Data SELECT. Should include its own ORDER BY (no UNION; no
    '              synthetic add row in the SQL - this routine prepends it).
    '              Column 1 should be the bound PK (matches helper convention).
    '   addLabel   Text shown in column 2 of the synthetic Add row. Column 1
    '              gets ADD_NEW_ID (-1) per convention.
    '
    ' IMPORTANT - Access ListBox.AddItem treats BOTH ";" and the locale list
    ' separator (often ",") as column delimiters, and Access ListBox does NOT
    ' have a SeparatorCharacters property to control that (only ComboBox does).
    ' This routine therefore strips both ";" and "," from value text before
    ' joining. The cosmetic cost is that currency formatting like "$32,000.00"
    ' renders as "$32000.00". If a caller wants comma-grouped numbers, they'd
    ' need to switch back to BuildAddableRowSource (Table/Query row source).

    Dim rs As ADODB.Recordset
    Set rs = New ADODB.Recordset
    rs.Open sql, CurrentProject.Connection, adOpenStatic, adLockReadOnly

    lst.RowSource = ""

    Dim fldCount As Long
    fldCount = rs.Fields.count
    If fldCount < 2 Then
        Err.Raise vbObjectError + 2003, "PopulateAddableListBoxFromAdo", _
                  "SQL must return at least 2 columns (PK + display)."
    End If

    Dim parts() As String
    ReDim parts(fldCount - 1)
    Dim j As Long

    ' Header row.
    For j = 0 To fldCount - 1
        parts(j) = SanitizeForValueList(rs.Fields(j).name)
    Next j
    lst.AddItem Join(parts, ";")

    ' Synthetic Add row.
    parts(0) = CStr(ADD_NEW_ID)
    parts(1) = SanitizeForValueList(addLabel)
    For j = 2 To fldCount - 1
        parts(j) = ""
    Next j
    lst.AddItem Join(parts, ";")

    ' Data rows.
    Do While Not rs.EOF
        For j = 0 To fldCount - 1
            parts(j) = SanitizeForValueList(CStr(Nz(rs.Fields(j).Value, "")))
        Next j
        lst.AddItem Join(parts, ";")
        rs.MoveNext
    Loop

    rs.Close
    Set rs = Nothing
End Sub


' Strips characters that Access ListBox.AddItem (with Value List row source)
' treats as column separators - "," and ";" specifically. Used by the AddItem
' code path; the BuildAddableRowSource code path is unaffected.
Private Function SanitizeForValueList(ByVal s As String) As String
    Dim out As String
    out = Replace(s, ",", "")
    out = Replace(out, ";", "")
    SanitizeForValueList = out
End Function
